title.en: Introduction to Road Safety in Rwanda
title.rw: Intangiriro ku mutekano wo mu muhanda mu Rwanda

description.en: Learn the meaning, principles and importance of road safety and responsible road use.
description.rw: Sobanukirwa igisobanuro cy'umutekano wo mu muhanda, amahame yawo n'inshingano z'abawukoresha.

definition.en: Road safety is the set of laws, practices, knowledge and precautions intended to prevent road crashes and protect drivers, passengers, pedestrians, cyclists and other road users.
definition.rw: Umutekano wo mu muhanda ni ihuriro ry'amategeko, imyitwarire, ubumenyi n'ingamba bigamije gukumira impanuka no kurinda abatwara ibinyabiziga, abagenzi, abanyamaguru, abatwara amagare n'abandi bose bakoresha umuhanda.

body.en:
1. Shared responsibility: A public road is used by different people. Drivers must control their vehicles, pedestrians must cross carefully, and passengers must avoid distracting drivers. Every person has a responsibility to respect other road users.

2. Obeying the law: Road users must follow traffic signs, signals, road markings and instructions from authorised traffic officers. Rwanda's Law No. 014/2026 of 6 March 2026 governs road traffic and aims to prevent road crashes.

3. Preparing for a journey: Drivers should check the general condition of their vehicles, including tyres, brakes, lights and other important safety components. They should also ensure that required documents and safety equipment are available.

4. Responsible behaviour: Patience, attention, respect and good judgement reduce dangerous situations. Drivers should not allow fatigue, distraction or unsafe behaviour to affect their decisions.

5. Protecting vulnerable road users: Children, pedestrians, cyclists and people with disabilities may need additional care and consideration. Drivers should remain alert around schools, markets, residential areas and pedestrian crossings.
body.rw:
1. Inshingano zisangiwe: Umuhanda nyabagendwa ukoreshwa n'abantu batandukanye. Abashoferi bagomba kugenzura ibinyabiziga, abanyamaguru bakambuka bitonze, naho abagenzi bakirinda kurangaza abashoferi. Buri wese afite inshingano zo kubaha abandi bakoresha umuhanda.

2. Kubahiriza amategeko: Abakoresha umuhanda bagomba gukurikiza ibyapa, amatara, ibimenyetso bishushanyije mu muhanda n'amabwiriza atangwa n'abakozi babifitiye ububasha. Itegeko n° 014/2026 ryo ku wa 6 Werurwe 2026 rigenga ikoreshwa ry'umuhanda mu Rwanda kandi rigamije gukumira impanuka.

3. Gutegura urugendo: Abashoferi bagomba kugenzura uko ibinyabiziga bimeze, harimo amapine, feri, amatara n'ibindi bikoresho by'umutekano. Bagomba no kureba ko bafite ibyangombwa n'ibikoresho bisabwa.

4. Imyitwarire iboneye: Kwihangana, kwitonda, kubaha abandi no gufata ibyemezo neza bigabanya ibyago. Umushoferi ntagomba kwemera ko umunaniro, kurangara cyangwa imyitwarire idatekanye bigira ingaruka ku byo akora.

5. Kurinda abakoresha umuhanda bashobora guhura n'ibyago byoroshye: Abana, abanyamaguru, abatwara amagare n'abantu bafite ubumuga bashobora gukenera kwitabwaho by'umwihariko. Abashoferi bagomba kwitonda hafi y'amashuri, amasoko, aho abantu batuye n'ahambukira abanyamaguru.

en: Road safety is everyone's responsibility.
Obey official traffic signs and instructions.
Check vehicle safety before travelling.
Avoid distraction and dangerous behaviour.
Protect pedestrians and other vulnerable road users.
rw: Umutekano wo mu muhanda ni inshingano ya buri wese.
Rengera abanyamaguru n'abandi bashobora guhura n'ibyago.

conclusion.en: Road safety depends on knowledge, discipline and cooperation. Every responsible action can help prevent crashes and protect lives.
conclusion.rw: Umutekano wo mu muhanda ushingira ku bumenyi, ikinyabupfura n'ubufatanye. Buri gikorwa cyiza gishobora gufasha gukumira impanuka no kurengera ubuzima.

quiz_connection.en: You should be able to explain road safety, identify the responsibilities of different road users and describe ways of preventing crashes.
quiz_connection.rw: Ugomba kuba ushobora gusobanura umutekano wo mu muhanda, kugaragaza inshingano z'abawukoresha no kuvuga uburyo bwo gukumira impanuka.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Road safety means the laws, knowledge and responsible actions used to prevent road crashes and protect everyone using roads.

DETAILED LESSON
Road safety is a shared responsibility. Drivers, passengers, pedestrians and cyclists must all behave responsibly. Drivers should maintain their vehicles, obey traffic signs and remain attentive. Pedestrians should use appropriate walking areas and cross carefully. Passengers should avoid distracting drivers. Children and people with disabilities may require additional protection. Rwanda's Law No. 014/2026 of 6 March 2026 provides the current general legal framework governing road traffic. Good road safety practices include preparation, patience, attention and respect.

CONCLUSION
A safe road environment is created when everyone understands and fulfils their responsibilities.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Umutekano wo mu muhanda ni amategeko, ubumenyi n'ibikorwa byiza bikoreshwa mu gukumira impanuka no kurinda abantu bose bakoresha umuhanda.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Umutekano wo mu muhanda ni inshingano ya buri wese. Abashoferi, abagenzi, abanyamaguru n'abatwara amagare bagomba kwitwara neza. Abashoferi bagomba kwita ku binyabiziga, kubahiriza ibyapa no kwibanda ku muhanda. Abanyamaguru bagomba gukoresha inzira zabagenewe no kwambuka bitonze. Abagenzi bagomba kwirinda kurangaza abashoferi. Abana n'abantu bafite ubumuga bashobora gukenera kurindwa by'umwihariko. Itegeko n° 014/2026 ryo ku wa 6 Werurwe 2026 ni ryo riteganya urwego rusange rw'amategeko agenga ikoreshwa ry'umuhanda mu Rwanda. Imyitwarire myiza irimo kwitegura, kwihangana, kwitonda no kubaha abandi.

UMWANZURO
Umuhanda utekanye ugerwaho iyo buri wese asobanukiwe inshingano ze kandi akazubahiriza.

title.rw: Ibyapa byo mu muhanda n'akamaro kabyo

description.en: Study the purpose, types, shapes and importance of official road signs.
description.rw: Iga intego, ibyiciro, imiterere n'akamaro k'ibyapa byemewe byo mu muhanda.

definition.en: A road sign is an officially recognised visual instruction, warning or information symbol placed beside or above a road to guide and regulate road users.
definition.rw: Icyapa cyo mu muhanda ni ikimenyetso cyemewe gishyirwa iruhande cyangwa hejuru y'umuhanda kigamije gutanga amabwiriza, kuburira cyangwa kumenyesha abakoresha umuhanda.

body.en:
1. Warning signs: These alert drivers to possible hazards ahead, such as bends, steep slopes, road works, slippery roads and pedestrian crossings. Their purpose is to encourage early attention and careful driving.

2. Regulatory signs: These communicate requirements and restrictions that road users must obey. Examples include stop, give-way, speed restrictions and prohibited movements. The exact meaning must be understood from the official sign.

3. Information signs: These help people identify directions, destinations, public facilities and useful services. They may indicate towns, hospitals, parking areas or other locations.

4. Understanding signs: Drivers should observe signs early, recognise their symbols and respond safely. They should not wait until the last moment to make a decision.

5. Legal importance: Official traffic signs are part of the road traffic control system. A sign should be interpreted according to the applicable Rwandan rules and its official design, not by guessing from its colour alone.
body.rw:
1. Ibyapa biburira: Bimenyesha umushoferi ibyago bishobora kuba imbere, nk'umuhanda uhetamye, ahazamuka cyangwa hamanuka cyane, ahari imirimo yo gusana umuhanda, ahanyerera n'ahambukira abanyamaguru. Bigamije gutuma umushoferi yitegura hakiri kare kandi akitonda.

2. Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza: Bitanga amabwiriza n'ibibujijwe abakoresha umuhanda bagomba kubahiriza. Ingero ni icyapa cyo guhagarara, icyo gutanga inzira, icyerekana umuvuduko ntarengwa n'icyo kubuza igikorwa runaka. Icyapa kigomba gusobanurwa hakurikijwe igishushanyo cyacyo cyemewe.

3. Ibyapa bitanga amakuru: Bifasha abantu kumenya icyerekezo, aho bajya, ibigo rusange na serivisi. Bishobora kwerekana imijyi, ibitaro, aho guhagarika ibinyabiziga n'ahandi.

4. Gusobanukirwa ibyapa: Umushoferi agomba kubona icyapa hakiri kare, kumenya ikimenyetso kiriho no kugikurikiza mu mutekano. Ntagomba gutegereza akanya ka nyuma ngo afate icyemezo.

5. Agaciro mu mategeko: Ibyapa byemewe ni kimwe mu bikoresho bigenga ikoreshwa ry'umuhanda. Bigomba gusobanurwa hakurikijwe amategeko akurikizwa mu Rwanda n'imiterere yabyo yemewe, aho gukeka ibisobanuro hashingiwe ku ibara gusa.

en: Warning signs alert road users to hazards.
Regulatory signs communicate rules and restrictions.
Information signs provide directions and useful information.
Recognise the complete symbol, not just its colour.
Obey official signs and instructions.
rw: Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza bitanga amabwiriza.
Menya ikimenyetso cyose, ntushingire ku ibara gusa.

conclusion.en: Road signs make traffic more organised and predictable. Understanding their official meaning helps prevent dangerous decisions.
conclusion.rw: Ibyapa bituma urujya n'uruza rutungana kandi rukamenyekana. Gusobanukirwa ibisobanuro byabyo byemewe bifasha gukumira ibyemezo biteje ibyago.

quiz_connection.en: Practise identifying warning, regulatory and information signs and explaining the correct response to each.
quiz_connection.rw: Itoze gutandukanya ibyapa biburira, bitegeka n'iby'amakuru no gusobanura uko ugomba kubyitwaramo.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Road signs are official visual messages used to warn, instruct and guide road users.

DETAILED LESSON
The main learning groups are warning signs, regulatory signs and information signs. Warning signs identify possible hazards. Regulatory signs communicate rules and restrictions. Information signs help road users identify destinations and services. A driver should observe each sign early and understand its complete symbol. Signs must be interpreted according to official Rwandan road regulations.

CONCLUSION
Understanding road signs is essential for safe and responsible road use.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Ibyapa ni ubutumwa bugaragara bukoreshwa mu kuburira, guha amabwiriza no kuyobora abakoresha umuhanda.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Ibyapa bigabanyijemo ibyapa biburira, ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza, n'ibyapa bitanga amakuru. Ibyapa biburira bigaragaza ibyago bishobora kuba. Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza bitanga amabwiriza. Ibyapa by'amakuru bifasha kumenya aho umuntu ajya na serivisi zihari. Umushoferi agomba kureba buri cyapa hakiri kare no gusobanukirwa ikimenyetso cyacyo cyose. Ibyapa bigomba gusobanurwa hakurikijwe amategeko y'umuhanda akurikizwa mu Rwanda.

UMWANZURO
Gusobanukirwa ibyapa ni ingenzi mu gukoresha umuhanda neza kandi mu mutekano.

title.rw: Ibyapa biburira n'ibyago byo mu muhanda

description.en: Learn how warning signs help drivers recognise hazards and prepare safely.
description.rw: Menya uko ibyapa biburira bifasha abashoferi kumenya ibyago no kubyitegurira.

definition.en: A warning sign is a traffic sign that alerts road users to a possible hazard or unusual road condition ahead.
definition.rw: Icyapa kiburira ni icyapa cyo mu muhanda kimenyekanisha ibyago bishobora kuba cyangwa imiterere idasanzwe y'umuhanda uri imbere.

body.en:
Warning signs are intended to give road users advance information. A bend sign indicates that the road changes direction. A steep-gradient warning indicates a significant uphill or downhill section. Road-work warnings alert drivers to workers, machinery or changed traffic arrangements. Slippery-road warnings indicate that vehicle control may be more difficult. Pedestrian and school warnings remind drivers that people may enter or cross the road.

When a warning sign is seen, the driver should observe the surrounding road, assess the conditions and adjust speed and attention appropriately. The driver should avoid sudden braking, unsafe overtaking and abrupt changes of direction. Weather, visibility and the behaviour of other road users should also be considered.

A warning sign does not give permission to ignore other rules. Drivers must continue to obey applicable speed limits, traffic signals and instructions.
body.rw:
Ibyapa biburira bigamije guha abakoresha umuhanda amakuru mbere y'uko bagera ahantu hashobora kuba ibyago. Icyapa cy'umuhanda uhetamye kigaragaza ko umuhanda uhindura icyerekezo. Icyapa cy'ahazamuka cyangwa hamanuka cyane kimenyesha ko hari igice cy'umuhanda gifite umusozi ukomeye. Icyapa cy'imirimo yo gusana umuhanda kimenyesha ko hashobora kuba abakozi, imashini cyangwa impinduka mu buryo bwo kugenda. Icyapa cy'umuhanda unyerera kigaragaza ko kugenzura ikinyabiziga bishobora kugorana. Ibyapa by'abanyamaguru n'iby'amashuri byibutsa abashoferi ko abantu bashobora kwinjira mu muhanda cyangwa kuwambuka.

Iyo ubonye icyapa kiburira, genzura umuhanda, suzuma uko ibintu bimeze kandi uhindure umuvuduko n'uko wita ku muhanda uko bikwiye. Irinde gufata feri mu buryo butunguranye, kunyuranaho ahateje ibyago no guhindura icyerekezo utunguranye. Ugomba no kuzirikana ikirere, uko umuhanda ugaragara n'imyitwarire y'abandi.

Icyapa kiburira ntiguha uburenganzira bwo kwirengagiza andi mategeko. Komeza kubahiriza umuvuduko wemewe, amatara n'amabwiriza.

en: Warning signs give advance notice of hazards.
Road works may change normal traffic conditions.
Slippery surfaces require extra care.
School and pedestrian warnings call for attention.
Warning signs do not cancel other traffic rules.
rw: Ibyapa biburira bimenyesha ibyago hakiri kare.
Imirimo yo gusana umuhanda ishobora guhindura uko ugendwamo.
Ibyapa biburira ntibikuraho andi mategeko y'umuhanda.

conclusion.en: Warning signs help prevent crashes by giving road users time to recognise and respond to hazards.
conclusion.rw: Ibyapa biburira bifasha gukumira impanuka kuko biha abakoresha umuhanda igihe cyo kumenya ibyago no kubyitwaramo.

quiz_connection.en: Identify the hazard shown by a warning sign and select the safest general response.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya akaga kagaragazwa n'icyapa kiburira kandi uhitemo uburyo bwiza bwo kukirinda.

content.en:
DEFINITION
A warning sign alerts road users to a possible hazard or unusual road condition ahead.

DETAILED LESSON
Warning signs may indicate bends, steep slopes, road works, slippery surfaces, schools or pedestrian crossings. They give drivers time to recognise a hazard and prepare. Drivers should remain attentive, assess conditions and follow all applicable rules. A warning sign does not replace a traffic instruction or speed restriction.

CONCLUSION
Recognising warning signs early helps drivers respond carefully and protect other road users.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Icyapa kiburira kimenyekanisha ibyago bishobora kuba cyangwa imiterere idasanzwe y'umuhanda uri imbere.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Ibyapa biburira bishobora kugaragaza umuhanda uhetamye, ahazamuka cyangwa hamanuka, imirimo yo gusana umuhanda, ahanyerera, amashuri cyangwa ahambukira abanyamaguru. Bifasha umushoferi kumenya akaga no kukitegurira. Umushoferi agomba kwitonda, gusuzuma uko umuhanda umeze no gukurikiza andi mategeko. Icyapa kiburira ntigisimbura amabwiriza cyangwa icyapa cy'umuvuduko.

UMWANZURO
Kumenya ibyapa biburira hakiri kare bifasha umushoferi kwitwara neza no kurinda abandi.

description.en: Understand signs that establish traffic requirements, restrictions and prohibitions.
description.rw: Sobanukirwa ibyapa bishyiraho amabwiriza, ibibujijwe n'ibisabwa mu muhanda.

definition.en: Regulatory signs are official signs that communicate traffic rules, obligations, restrictions or prohibitions.
definition.rw: Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza ni ibyapa byemewe bitanga amategeko, inshingano, imipaka cyangwa ibikorwa bibujijwe mu muhanda.

body.en:
Regulatory signs are important because they establish how road users must behave in particular places. A STOP sign requires the driver to stop as required by the applicable rules before proceeding. A give-way sign communicates the obligation to yield to traffic that has priority. Speed-limit signs communicate the maximum permitted speed for the indicated section, subject to other applicable conditions. Prohibition signs may restrict entry, turning, overtaking or parking.

Drivers should identify the sign, understand its official meaning and comply with it. They must not assume that a road is unrestricted simply because no other vehicle is visible. Temporary regulatory signs and instructions at road works should also be taken seriously.

Where a driver is uncertain about a sign, the safe approach is to avoid making an assumption and to seek clarification from an authoritative road-safety learning resource.
body.rw:
Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza ni ingenzi kuko bigena uko abakoresha umuhanda bagomba kwitwara ahantu runaka. Icyapa cyo guhagarara gisaba umushoferi guhagarara nk'uko amategeko abiteganya mbere yo gukomeza. Icyapa cyo gutanga inzira kigaragaza inshingano yo guha inzira abafite uburenganzira bwo kubanza. Icyapa cy'umuvuduko ntarengwa kigaragaza umuvuduko ntarengwa wemewe kuri icyo gice cy'umuhanda, hakurikijwe n'ibindi bisabwa. Ibyapa bibuza bishobora kubuza kwinjira, gukata, kunyuranaho cyangwa guhagarika ikinyabiziga.

Abashoferi bagomba kumenya icyapa, gusobanukirwa igisobanuro cyacyo cyemewe no kugikurikiza. Ntibagomba kwibwira ko nta mabwiriza ahari kubera gusa ko nta kindi kinyabiziga babona. Ibyapa by'agateganyo n'amabwiriza ashyirwa ahari imirimo yo gusana umuhanda na byo bigomba kubahirizwa.

Iyo umushoferi adasobanukiwe icyapa, agomba kwirinda kugihimbira ibisobanuro ahubwo akifashisha inyandiko zizewe z'umutekano wo mu muhanda.

en: Regulatory signs communicate enforceable traffic requirements.
STOP and give-way signs have different meanings.
Speed-limit signs must be respected.
Prohibition signs restrict specified actions.
Temporary signs must also be observed.
rw: Ibyapa bitegeka bitanga amabwiriza agomba kubahirizwa.
Icyapa cyo guhagarara gitandukanye n'icyo gutanga inzira.
Ibyapa by'agateganyo na byo bigomba gukurikizwa.

conclusion.en: Regulatory signs organise traffic by clearly communicating what road users must do or must not do.
conclusion.rw: Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza bitunganya urujya n'uruza bigaragaza neza ibyo abakoresha umuhanda bagomba gukora cyangwa kwirinda.

quiz_connection.en: Distinguish STOP, give-way, speed-limit and prohibition signs and explain the action required by each.
quiz_connection.rw: Tandukanya ibyapa byo guhagarara, gutanga inzira, umuvuduko ntarengwa n'ibibujijwe, usobanure icyo buri kimwe gisaba.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Regulatory signs communicate official traffic rules, obligations and restrictions.

DETAILED LESSON
STOP signs, give-way signs, speed restrictions and prohibition signs are examples of regulatory signs. Each has a specific meaning. Drivers should understand the sign and follow the required instruction. Temporary restrictions around road works must also be respected. Never guess the meaning of an unfamiliar official sign.

CONCLUSION
Regulatory signs help road users understand their duties and avoid conflicts.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Ibyapa bitegeka cyangwa bibuza bitanga amategeko, inshingano n'ibibujijwe byemewe mu muhanda.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Ibyapa byo guhagarara, gutanga inzira, kugabanya umuvuduko no kubuza ibikorwa ni ingero z'ibyapa bitegeka. Buri cyapa gifite igisobanuro cyihariye. Abashoferi bagomba kugisobanukirwa no gukurikiza amabwiriza yacyo. Ibibujijwe by'agateganyo hafi y'ahari imirimo yo gusana umuhanda na byo bigomba kubahirizwa. Ntukakeke ibisobanuro by'icyapa utazi.

UMWANZURO
Ibyapa bitegeka bifasha abakoresha umuhanda kumenya inshingano zabo no kwirinda amakimbirane.

title.rw: Amatara yo mu muhanda n'uko agenga urujya n'uruza

description.en: Learn the purpose of traffic signals and the importance of responding correctly.
description.rw: Menya intego z'amatara yo mu muhanda n'akamaro ko kuyakurikiza neza.

definition.en: Traffic lights are electronic or illuminated signals used to control the movement of vehicles and pedestrians at specified road locations.
definition.rw: Amatara yo mu muhanda ni ibimenyetso bitanga amabwiriza hakoreshejwe urumuri bigenga uko ibinyabiziga n'abanyamaguru bagenda ahantu runaka.

body.en:
Red, amber and green are commonly used traffic signal colours. Red communicates STOP. Green generally permits movement when the road is clear and the movement is safe. Amber warns that the signal is changing, and road users must respond according to the applicable traffic rules.

Drivers should observe the signal before entering an intersection. They should not enter a junction merely because another vehicle has started moving. Pedestrians should use pedestrian signals where provided and should not assume that vehicles will stop automatically.

A green signal does not remove the duty to look for pedestrians, cyclists or vehicles that may still be clearing the junction. If a traffic signal is not working, road users should follow the applicable signs, road rules and directions of an authorised officer rather than inventing a rule.
body.rw:
Amatara atukura, umuhondo n'icyatsi ni yo akoreshwa cyane mu kugenga urujya n'uruza. Itara ritukura risobanura GUKUMA. Icyatsi muri rusange cyemerera gukomeza iyo umuhanda ufunguye kandi nta kaga. Umuhondo ugaragaza ko ibimenyetso bigiye guhinduka, bityo abakoresha umuhanda bakagomba kubyitwaramo bakurikije amategeko akurikizwa.

Abashoferi bagomba kureba itara mbere yo kwinjira aho imihanda ihurira. Ntibagomba kwinjira mu ihuriro ry'imihanda kubera gusa ko ikindi kinyabiziga cyatangiye kugenda. Abanyamaguru bagomba gukurikiza amatara yabagenewe igihe ahari kandi ntibatekereze ko ibinyabiziga bizahita bihagarara.

Itara ry'icyatsi ntirikuraho inshingano yo kureba abanyamaguru, abatwara amagare cyangwa ibinyabiziga bishobora kuba bitararangiza kunyura mu ihuriro. Iyo itara ridakora, abakoresha umuhanda bagomba gukurikiza ibyapa, amategeko n'amabwiriza y'umukozi ubifitiye ububasha aho kwihimbira itegeko.

en: Red means stop.
Green permits movement only when safe.
Amber indicates a change in the signal.
Always observe pedestrians and other traffic.
Follow authorised instructions if signals fail.
rw: Icyatsi cyemerera gukomeza iyo nta kaga.
Buri gihe genzura abanyamaguru n'ibindi binyabiziga.
Kurikiza amabwiriza yemewe iyo amatara adakora.

conclusion.en: Traffic lights coordinate movement, reduce conflicts and help protect people at intersections.
conclusion.rw: Amatara yo mu muhanda ahuza urujya n'uruza, akagabanya amakimbirane kandi akarinda abantu aho imihanda ihurira.

quiz_connection.en: Explain the meaning of red, amber and green signals and identify safe actions at an intersection.
quiz_connection.rw: Sobanura ibisobanuro by'umutuku, umuhondo n'icyatsi kandi umenye imyitwarire itekanye aho imihanda ihurira.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Traffic lights are illuminated signals that control the movement of road users.

DETAILED LESSON
Red means stop. Green generally permits movement when it is safe and the way is clear. Amber warns that the signal is changing. Drivers must observe intersections carefully and remain alert to pedestrians and other vehicles. If signals are not working, follow applicable traffic rules and authorised directions.

CONCLUSION
Correct use of traffic lights helps organise traffic and prevent crashes.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Amatara yo mu muhanda ni ibimenyetso by'urumuri bigenga urujya n'uruza rw'abakoresha umuhanda.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Umutuku usobanura guhagarara. Icyatsi muri rusange cyemerera gukomeza iyo ari umutekano kandi inzira ifunguye. Umuhondo ugaragaza ko itara rigiye guhinduka. Abashoferi bagomba kugenzura aho imihanda ihurira no kwitondera abanyamaguru n'ibindi binyabiziga. Iyo amatara adakora, kurikiza amategeko n'amabwiriza yemewe.

UMWANZURO
Gukurikiza amatara neza bitunganya urujya n'uruza kandi bikarinda impanuka.

title.rw: Imirongo yo mu muhanda no kugendera mu murongo wabugenewe

description.en: Understand road lines, pedestrian crossings, lane boundaries and their safety functions.
description.rw: Sobanukirwa imirongo yo mu muhanda, ahambukira abanyamaguru n'imbibi z'imihanda y'ibinyabiziga.

definition.en: Road markings are lines, symbols and words applied to the road surface to organise traffic, indicate restrictions and guide road users.
definition.rw: Imirongo yo mu muhanda ni imirongo, ibimenyetso n'amagambo bishushanywa ku buso bw'umuhanda bigamije gutunganya urujya n'uruza, kugaragaza ibibujijwe no kuyobora abakoresha umuhanda.

body.en:
Road markings help drivers understand lane boundaries and where particular movements are allowed or restricted. Broken lines generally indicate that a crossing or lane change may be permitted when safe and lawful. Continuous lines may impose restrictions on crossing or changing lanes. The exact legal meaning depends on the applicable road markings and regulations.

Pedestrian crossings identify places intended for pedestrians to cross. Drivers should observe these areas and respect pedestrian priority as provided by the law. Stop lines show where vehicles are required to stop in response to a signal or instruction.

Before changing lanes, drivers should observe the road, check mirrors and blind spots where applicable, signal their intention and ensure that the movement is permitted and safe. Road markings must be considered together with signs and traffic signals.
body.rw:
Imirongo yo mu muhanda ifasha abashoferi kumenya imbibi z'imihanda y'ibinyabiziga n'ahantu ibikorwa bimwe byemewe cyangwa bibujijwe. Imirongo icagaguye muri rusange ishobora kwerekana ko kwambuka cyangwa guhindura umurongo byemewe iyo nta kaga kandi amategeko abyemera. Imirongo idacagaguye ishobora gushyiraho ibibujijwe mu kwambuka cyangwa guhindura umurongo. Igisobanuro cyayo nyacyo gishingira ku bimenyetso n'amategeko akurikizwa.

Imirongo y'abanyamaguru igaragaza ahagenewe kwambukira. Abashoferi bagomba kwitondera aho hantu no kubahiriza uburenganzira bw'abanyamaguru nk'uko amategeko abiteganya. Umurongo wo guhagararaho werekana aho ikinyabiziga kigomba guhagarara bitewe n'itara cyangwa amabwiriza.

Mbere yo guhindura umurongo, umushoferi agomba kureba umuhanda, kugenzura mu ndorerwamo no kureba ahantu atabona neza igihe bikenewe, kwerekana icyerekezo no kwemeza ko icyo gikorwa cyemewe kandi gitekanye. Imirongo igomba gusuzumwa hamwe n'ibyapa n'amatara.

en: Road markings organise lanes and movements.
Broken and continuous lines may have different meanings.
Pedestrian crossings identify crossing areas.
Stop lines show where vehicles should stop.
Check carefully before changing lanes.
rw: Imirongo itunganya inzira n'uko ibinyabiziga bigenda.
Imirongo icagaguye n'idacagaguye ishobora kugira ibisobanuro bitandukanye.
Umurongo wo guhagararaho werekana aho ikinyabiziga gihagarara.
Genzura neza mbere yo guhindura umurongo.

conclusion.en: Road markings provide important visual guidance and help road users share available space safely.
conclusion.rw: Imirongo yo mu muhanda itanga amabwiriza agaragara kandi igafasha abantu gusaranganya inzira mu mutekano.

quiz_connection.en: Identify common road markings and explain their general purpose and safety importance.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya imirongo isanzwe yo mu muhanda kandi usobanure icyo igamije n'akamaro kayo mu mutekano.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Road markings are lines and symbols placed on road surfaces to guide traffic.

DETAILED LESSON
Road markings show lane boundaries, stop lines and pedestrian crossings. Different line patterns can indicate different permissions or restrictions. Drivers must follow the official meaning and check carefully before changing lanes. Road markings work together with traffic signs and signals.

CONCLUSION
Understanding road markings helps prevent confusion and unsafe movements.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Imirongo yo mu muhanda ni imirongo n'ibimenyetso bishyirwa ku buso bw'umuhanda kugira ngo biyobore urujya n'uruza.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Imirongo igaragaza imbibi z'inzira, ahagenewe guhagarara n'ahambukira abanyamaguru. Imiterere itandukanye y'imirongo ishobora kugaragaza ibinyuranye byemewe cyangwa bibujijwe. Abashoferi bagomba gukurikiza ibisobanuro byemewe no kugenzura neza mbere yo guhindura umurongo. Imirongo ikorana n'ibyapa n'amatara yo mu muhanda.

UMWANZURO
Gusobanukirwa imirongo yo mu muhanda bifasha gukumira urujijo n'ibikorwa biteje ibyago.

title.en: Driving on the Correct Side of the Road in Rwanda
title.rw: Kugendera ku ruhande rukwiye rw'umuhanda mu Rwanda

description.en: Learn the legal driving side in Rwanda and why lane discipline matters.
description.rw: Menya uruhande rwemewe ibinyabiziga bigenderamo mu Rwanda n'akamaro ko kubahiriza inzira.

definition.en: The driving side is the side of the road on which vehicles are legally required to travel.
definition.rw: Uruhande rugenderwamo ni uruhande rw'umuhanda amategeko ateganya ko ibinyabiziga bigenderamo.

body.en:
Article 4 of Rwanda's Law No. 014/2026 of 6 March 2026 states that vehicles travel on the right-hand side of the road. This is an important rule for organising traffic and reducing conflicts between vehicles travelling in opposite directions.

Drivers should maintain their proper position and follow lane markings, traffic signs and authorised instructions. They should not use the opposing side of the road unless a lawful manoeuvre permits it and the movement can be completed safely.

Drivers must pay attention when approaching intersections, bends and areas where the road becomes narrower. They should also consider pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles entering from side roads. Lane discipline helps make road movements more predictable.
body.rw:
Ingingo ya 4 y'Itegeko n° 014/2026 ryo ku wa 6 Werurwe 2026 rigenga ikoreshwa ry'umuhanda ivuga ko ibinyabiziga bigendera ku ruhande rw'iburyo rw'umuhanda. Iri ni itegeko rikomeye mu gutunganya urujya n'uruza no kugabanya amakimbirane hagati y'ibinyabiziga bigenda mu byerekezo bitandukanye.

Abashoferi bagomba kugendera mu mwanya wabugenewe kandi bagakurikiza imirongo, ibyapa n'amabwiriza yemewe. Ntibagomba gukoresha uruhande rw'abaturutse imbere keretse igikorwa runaka cyemewe n'amategeko kandi gishobora gukorwa mu mutekano.

Abashoferi bagomba kwitonda bageze aho imihanda ihurira, mu makoni no mu bice umuhanda ugabanukiramo. Bagomba no kwitondera abanyamaguru, abatwara amagare n'ibinyabiziga byinjira biva mu mihanda mito. Kugendera mu murongo ukwiye bituma urujya n'uruza ruteganyirika.

en: Rwanda's Law No. 014/2026 Article 4 requires vehicles to travel on the right.
Follow lane markings and official instructions.
Do not use the opposing side unlawfully.
Take extra care at bends and intersections.
Lane discipline helps prevent conflicts.
rw: Ingingo ya 4 y'Itegeko n° 014/2026 isaba ibinyabiziga kugendera iburyo.
Ntukoreshe uruhande rw'abaturutse imbere mu buryo bunyuranyije n'amategeko.
Kugendera mu murongo ukwiye bifasha gukumira impanuka.

conclusion.en: Driving on the right is a legal requirement in Rwanda. Correct lane discipline supports predictable and safer traffic.
conclusion.rw: Kugendera iburyo ni itegeko mu Rwanda. Kubahiriza inzira bikomeza gutuma urujya n'uruza ruteganyirika kandi ruba rufite umutekano.

quiz_connection.en: Remember the driving side required by Article 4 of Law No. 014/2026.
quiz_connection.rw: Ibuka uruhande ibinyabiziga bigenderamo nk'uko biteganywa n'ingingo ya 4 y'Itegeko n° 014/2026.

content.en:
DEFINITION
The driving side is the side of the road on which vehicles must travel.

DETAILED LESSON
Article 4 of Rwanda's Law No. 014/2026 of 6 March 2026 establishes that vehicles travel on the right-hand side. Drivers must maintain proper lane discipline and follow road markings and instructions. They should avoid unlawful use of the opposing side and take care at bends and intersections.

CONCLUSION
Driving on the right is a legal requirement in Rwanda and helps organise traffic.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Uruhande rugenderwamo ni uruhande rw'umuhanda ibinyabiziga bigomba kugenderamo.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Ingingo ya 4 y'Itegeko n° 014/2026 ryo ku wa 6 Werurwe 2026 iteganya ko ibinyabiziga bigendera iburyo. Abashoferi bagomba kugendera mu nzira yabugenewe no gukurikiza imirongo n'amabwiriza. Bagomba kwirinda gukoresha uruhande rw'abaturutse imbere mu buryo butemewe no kwitonda mu makoni n'aho imihanda ihurira.

UMWANZURO
Kugendera iburyo ni itegeko mu Rwanda kandi bifasha gutunganya urujya n'uruza.

title.en: Pedestrian Safety and Safe Road Crossing

description.en: Learn safe walking habits and the responsibilities of drivers around pedestrians.
description.rw: Menya uburyo bwo kugenda n'amaguru mu mutekano n'inshingano z'abashoferi hafi y'abanyamaguru.

definition.en: Pedestrian safety refers to practices and road arrangements that protect people travelling on foot.
definition.rw: Umutekano w'abanyamaguru ni imyitwarire n'uburyo bwo gutunganya umuhanda bigamije kurinda abantu bawugendamo n'amaguru.

body.en:
Pedestrians should use sidewalks or designated walking areas where available. They should choose suitable crossing places and observe traffic before crossing. A pedestrian should not assume that an approaching driver has seen them or will stop automatically.

At marked crossings, drivers should be alert and follow the applicable pedestrian priority rules. They should be especially careful near schools, markets, hospitals and residential areas. Children may not judge vehicle speed and distance accurately, so adults should guide them when crossing busy roads.

Phones, headphones and other distractions can prevent pedestrians from noticing approaching traffic. Walking attentively and avoiding sudden entry into the road helps reduce danger. People with disabilities may require additional time and consideration when crossing.
body.rw:
Abanyamaguru bagomba gukoresha inzira zabagenewe igihe zihari. Bagomba guhitamo ahantu hemewe ho kwambukira no kureba ibinyabiziga mbere yo kwambuka. Umunyamaguru ntagomba kwibwira ko umushoferi umwegereye yamubonye cyangwa ko azahita ahagarara.

Ahambukira abanyamaguru hagaragajwe n'imirongo, abashoferi bagomba kwitonda no gukurikiza amategeko agenga uburenganzira bw'abanyamaguru. Bagomba kwitonda cyane hafi y'amashuri, amasoko, ibitaro n'aho abantu batuye. Abana bashobora kutamenya neza umuvuduko n'intera y'ikinyabiziga, bityo abantu bakuru bakabafasha igihe bambuka imihanda nyabagendwa.

Telefoni, utwuma two kumva umuziki n'ibindi bikurangaza bishobora gutuma umunyamaguru atabona ibinyabiziga bimusatira. Kugenda witeguye no kwirinda kwinjira mu muhanda utunguranye bifasha kugabanya ibyago. Abantu bafite ubumuga bashobora gukenera igihe n'ubufasha byihariye igihe bambuka.

en: Use pedestrian paths where available.
Observe traffic before crossing.
Drivers should be alert near crossings.
Children need adult guidance near busy roads.
Avoid distractions while walking.
rw: Abashoferi bagomba kwitonda hafi y'ahambukira abanyamaguru.
Abana bakeneye kuyoborwa n'abantu bakuru hafi y'imihanda nyabagendwa.

conclusion.en: Pedestrian safety requires attention from both pedestrians and drivers. Respect and careful observation protect lives.
conclusion.rw: Umutekano w'abanyamaguru usaba kwitonda kw'abanyamaguru n'abashoferi. Kubahana no kugenzura neza ibiri mu muhanda birengera ubuzima.

quiz_connection.en: Explain safe crossing behaviour and the responsibilities of drivers near pedestrian crossings.
quiz_connection.rw: Sobanura uburyo bwo kwambuka mu mutekano n'inshingano z'abashoferi hafi y'ahambukira abanyamaguru.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Pedestrian safety means protecting people who travel on foot.

DETAILED LESSON
Pedestrians should use designated walking areas, observe traffic and cross at appropriate places. Drivers should be alert near crossings, schools and markets. Children and people with disabilities may need additional consideration. Avoid distractions while walking and never assume that traffic has stopped.

CONCLUSION
Pedestrians and drivers must cooperate to protect people travelling on foot.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Umutekano w'abanyamaguru ni ukurinda abantu bagenda n'amaguru.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Abanyamaguru bagomba gukoresha inzira zabagenewe, kureba ibinyabiziga no kwambukira ahantu hemewe. Abashoferi bagomba kwitonda hafi y'ahambukira abanyamaguru, amashuri n'amasoko. Abana n'abantu bafite ubumuga bashobora gukenera kwitabwaho by'umwihariko. Irinde kurangara igihe ugenda n'amaguru kandi ntukibwire ko ibinyabiziga byahagaze.

UMWANZURO
Abanyamaguru n'abashoferi bagomba gufatanya kurinda abantu bagenda n'amaguru.

description.en: Learn responsible motorcycle use, protective equipment and passenger safety.
description.rw: Menya uko moto ikoreshwa neza, ibikoresho birinda umutekano n'uko umugenzi arindwa.

definition.en: Motorcycle safety consists of the precautions, equipment and responsible behaviours used to protect motorcycle riders, passengers and other road users.
definition.rw: Umutekano wa moto ugizwe n'ingamba, ibikoresho n'imyitwarire myiza bigamije kurinda uyitwaye, umugenzi n'abandi bakoresha umuhanda.

body.en:
Motorcycles provide transport and support many livelihoods, but riders and passengers are more exposed to the surrounding environment than occupants of enclosed vehicles. An appropriate protective helmet is an important safety measure for both the rider and passenger. It should fit correctly and be secured according to its instructions.

Before travelling, a rider should ensure that the motorcycle is in suitable working condition. Important components include tyres, brakes, lights, mirrors and the general steering system. The motorcycle should not carry more people or loads than legally permitted.

Riders should obey speed limits, traffic signs and road instructions. They should avoid distractions and dangerous manoeuvres, maintain awareness of pedestrians and never assume that other drivers have seen them. Rwanda National Police road-safety education also emphasises helmet use, respect for speed limits and avoiding phone use while riding.
body.rw:
Moto zitanga serivisi zo gutwara abantu kandi zigafasha abantu benshi mu mibereho yabo, ariko abazigenderamo baba bahuye n'ibiri hanze kurusha abari mu binyabiziga bifunze. Ingofero iboneye ni kimwe mu bikoresho by'ingenzi birinda uyitwaye n'umugenzi. Igomba kuba imukwiriye kandi ikambarwa hakurikijwe amabwiriza yayo.

Mbere y'urugendo, utwaye moto agomba kugenzura ko imeze neza. Ibice by'ingenzi birimo amapine, feri, amatara, indorerwamo n'uburyo bwo kuyobora moto. Moto ntigomba gutwara abantu cyangwa imizigo irenze ibyemewe n'amategeko.

Abatwara moto bagomba kubahiriza umuvuduko, ibyapa n'amabwiriza yo mu muhanda. Bagomba kwirinda ibibakurangaza n'ibikorwa biteje ibyago, kwita ku banyamaguru no kutibwira ko abandi bashoferi bababonye. Inyigisho z'umutekano zitangwa na Polisi y'u Rwanda na zo zishimangira kwambara ingofero, kubahiriza umuvuduko no kwirinda gukoresha telefoni utwaye moto.

en: Wear an appropriate helmet.
Check tyres, brakes, lights and mirrors.
Do not exceed legally permitted passenger or load limits.
Avoid phone distractions while riding.
Respect pedestrians and traffic rules.
rw: Nturenze umubare w'abagenzi cyangwa imizigo byemewe.

conclusion.en: Responsible motorcycle use requires protective equipment, a roadworthy motorcycle and respect for all traffic rules.
conclusion.rw: Gukoresha moto neza bisaba ibikoresho birinda umutekano, moto imeze neza no kubahiriza amategeko yose y'umuhanda.

quiz_connection.en: Identify motorcycle safety equipment and explain the responsibilities of riders and passengers.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya ibikoresho birinda umutekano wa moto kandi usobanure inshingano z'uyitwaye n'umugenzi.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Motorcycle safety means protecting riders, passengers and other road users through suitable equipment and responsible behaviour.

DETAILED LESSON
Motorcyclists and passengers should use appropriate helmets. Riders should check the motorcycle before travelling, obey traffic rules and avoid distraction. They must not carry more passengers or loads than permitted. Rwanda National Police promotes responsible riding, helmet use and respect for pedestrians.

CONCLUSION
A safe motorcycle journey depends on preparation, protective equipment and responsible riding.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Umutekano wa moto ni ukurinda uyitwaye, umugenzi n'abandi bakoresha umuhanda hakoreshejwe ibikoresho biboneye n'imyitwarire myiza.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Abatwara moto n'abagenzi bagomba gukoresha ingofero ziboneye. Utwaye moto agomba kuyigenzura mbere y'urugendo, kubahiriza amategeko no kwirinda kurangara. Ntagomba gutwara abagenzi cyangwa imizigo irenze ibyemewe. Polisi y'u Rwanda ishishikariza abatwara moto kwitwara neza, kwambara ingofero no kubaha abanyamaguru.

UMWANZURO
Urugendo rwa moto ruba rufite umutekano iyo umuntu yiteguye, yambaye ibikoresho birinda kandi yitwaye neza.

title.en: Seat Belts and Vehicle Occupant Protection
title.rw: Imikandara y'umutekano no kurinda abantu bari mu kinyabiziga

description.en: Understand how seat belts and suitable child restraints help protect vehicle occupants.
description.rw: Sobanukirwa uko imikandara n'intebe zabana birinda abantu bari mu kinyabiziga.

definition.en: A seat belt is a vehicle safety device designed to restrain an occupant and reduce the risk of injury during sudden vehicle movement or a collision.
definition.rw: Umukandara w'umutekano ni igikoresho kiri mu kinyabiziga kigamije gufata neza umuntu ukirimo no kugabanya ibyago byo gukomereka igihe ikinyabiziga gihagaze gitunguranye cyangwa habaye impanuka.

body.en:
Seat belts help keep occupants in their proper seating positions and reduce the chance of serious injury. Drivers and passengers should use the safety equipment provided in the vehicle according to the applicable law and manufacturer's instructions.

A seat belt should be fitted correctly, should not be twisted and should be adjusted so that it provides the intended protection. Children require suitable child-restraint arrangements appropriate to their size and the law. They should not be placed in unsuitable seating arrangements.

Airbags are additional protective systems. They are not a replacement for a seat belt. Vehicle occupants should also avoid carrying loose objects that could become dangerous during sudden braking. Drivers should ensure that passengers understand and use available safety equipment.
body.rw:
Imikandara ifasha abantu kuguma mu myanya yabo kandi ikagabanya ibyago byo gukomereka bikomeye. Abashoferi n'abagenzi bagomba gukoresha ibikoresho by'umutekano biri mu kinyabiziga hakurikijwe amategeko n'amabwiriza y'uwagikoze.

Umukandara ugomba kwambarwa neza, ntugoreke kandi ugahuzwa n'umubiri ku buryo urinda uko bikwiye. Abana bakeneye intebe cyangwa ibindi bikoresho bibagenewe hakurikijwe ingano yabo n'amategeko. Ntibagomba kwicazwa mu buryo butabereye umutekano wabo.

Imifuka y'umwuka irinda abantu ni ibikoresho byunganira umutekano. Ntisimbura umukandara. Abari mu kinyabiziga bagomba no kwirinda ibintu bitajegajega bishobora kubateza ibyago igihe ikinyabiziga gihagaritswe gitunguranye. Umushoferi agomba kwemeza ko abagenzi basobanukiwe kandi bakoresha ibikoresho by'umutekano bihari.

en: Seat belts help protect vehicle occupants.
Wear the belt correctly and avoid twisting it.
Children need suitable protective arrangements.
Airbags do not replace seat belts.
Follow applicable vehicle safety rules.
rw: Imikandara ifasha kurinda abantu bari mu kinyabiziga.
Abana bakeneye uburyo bwihariye bwo kubarinda.

conclusion.en: Seat belts and appropriate protective arrangements are essential parts of responsible vehicle use.
conclusion.rw: Imikandara n'ibikoresho biboneye byo kurinda abantu ni ingenzi mu gukoresha ikinyabiziga neza.

quiz_connection.en: Explain the purpose of seat belts and distinguish their role from that of airbags.
quiz_connection.rw: Sobanura akamaro k'umukandara kandi utandukanye umurimo wawo n'uw'imifuka y'umwuka.

content.en:
DEFINITION
A seat belt is a safety device that helps restrain a vehicle occupant and reduce injury risk.

DETAILED LESSON
Seat belts should be worn correctly by vehicle occupants according to applicable rules. They should not be twisted or incorrectly positioned. Children require suitable protective arrangements. Airbags provide additional protection but do not replace seat belts. Drivers should make sure passengers use available safety equipment.

CONCLUSION
Correct use of seat belts is an important part of protecting everyone travelling in a vehicle.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Umukandara w'umutekano ni igikoresho gifasha kurinda umuntu uri mu kinyabiziga no kugabanya ibyago byo gukomereka.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Abari mu kinyabiziga bagomba kwambara imikandara neza hakurikijwe amategeko. Ntigomba kugorekwa cyangwa kwambarwa nabi. Abana bakeneye ibikoresho bibarinda bibabereye. Imifuka y'umwuka yunganira umutekano ariko ntisimbura imikandara. Umushoferi agomba kureba ko abagenzi bakoresha ibikoresho by'umutekano bihari.

UMWANZURO
Gukoresha imikandara neza ni ingenzi mu kurinda abantu bose bari mu kinyabiziga.

title.rw: Ibibazo by'ubutabazi mu muhanda n'uko witwara

description.en: Learn safe and responsible actions when a road emergency or crash occurs.
description.rw: Menya ibikorwa by'umutekano n'inshingano igihe habaye impanuka cyangwa ikindi kibazo mu muhanda.

definition.en: A road emergency is an unexpected situation on or near a road that may threaten people's safety or require assistance from emergency services.
definition.rw: Ikibazo cy'ubutabazi mu muhanda ni ibintu bitunguranye bibereye mu muhanda cyangwa hafi yawo bishobora gushyira abantu mu kaga cyangwa bigasaba ubufasha bw'inzego z'ubutabazi.

body.en:
The first priority during a road emergency is to protect people from further danger. A person who arrives at an incident should avoid entering an unsafe area or creating additional risks. Emergency services should be contacted through the appropriate official channels.

If it is safe to do so, provide clear information about the location, the type of incident and the assistance required. Avoid crowding the scene, spreading unverified information or interfering with trained responders.

A person without first-aid training should not attempt procedures beyond their knowledge. Do not move an injured person unless there is an immediate danger or a trained responder directs it. Follow instructions from emergency personnel and cooperate with authorised officers.

After an incident, accurate information and responsible cooperation can assist the relevant authorities in handling the situation.
body.rw:
Ikintu cya mbere mu gihe habaye ikibazo mu muhanda ni ukurinda abantu kongera guhura n'akaga. Umuntu ugeze ahabereye ikibazo agomba kwirinda kwinjira ahantu hateje ibyago cyangwa kongera guteza ibindi bibazo. Inzego z'ubutabazi zigomba guhamagarwa hakoreshejwe inzira zemewe.

Iyo ari umutekano, tanga amakuru asobanutse ku hantu ikibazo cyabereye, ubwoko bwacyo n'ubufasha bukenewe. Irinde kugota ahabereye ikibazo, gukwirakwiza amakuru atagenzuwe cyangwa kubangamira abatabazi babihuguriwe.

Umuntu utaratojwe ubutabazi bw'ibanze ntagomba gukora ibikorwa birenze ubumenyi afite. Ntukimure umuntu wakomeretse keretse hari akaga kihutirwa cyangwa umutabazi wabihuguriwe abigusabye. Kurikiza amabwiriza y'abatabazi n'abakozi babifitiye ububasha.

Nyuma y'ikibazo, gutanga amakuru y'ukuri no gufatanya mu buryo buboneye bifasha inzego zibishinzwe kugikemura.

en: Protect people from further danger.
Contact appropriate emergency services.
Give accurate location and incident information.
Do not interfere with trained responders.
Do not attempt medical procedures beyond your training.
rw: Tanga amakuru y'ukuri ku hantu n'uko ikibazo giteye.
Ntukore ibikorwa by'ubuvuzi birenze ibyo wahuguweho.

conclusion.en: A calm, informed and responsible response helps protect people and allows trained emergency services to work effectively.
conclusion.rw: Kwifata, kugira amakuru no kwitwara neza bifasha kurinda abantu kandi bigatuma inzego z'ubutabazi zikora neza.

quiz_connection.en: Identify the first priorities during a road emergency and explain why trained responders should be allowed to work.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya iby'ingenzi bigomba gukorwa igihe habaye ikibazo mu muhanda kandi usobanure impamvu abatabazi babihuguriwe bagomba guhabwa umwanya wo gukora.

content.en:
DEFINITION
A road emergency is an unexpected road incident that may require urgent assistance.

DETAILED LESSON
Protect people from further danger, contact appropriate emergency services and provide accurate information. Do not crowd the scene or interfere with trained responders. People without first-aid training should avoid procedures beyond their knowledge. Follow authorised instructions.

CONCLUSION
Responsible action during an emergency can help protect lives and support effective rescue work.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Ikibazo cy'ubutabazi mu muhanda ni ibintu bitunguranye bishobora gusaba ubufasha bwihutirwa.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Rinda abantu kongera guhura n'akaga, hamagara inzego z'ubutabazi kandi utange amakuru y'ukuri. Ntukagose ahabereye ikibazo cyangwa ngo ubangamire abatabazi babihuguriwe. Abantu batatojwe ubutabazi bw'ibanze bagomba kwirinda ibikorwa birenze ubumenyi bwabo. Kurikiza amabwiriza yemewe.

UMWANZURO
Kwifata no kwitwara neza mu gihe cy'ikibazo bifasha kurinda ubuzima no korohereza abatabazi.

description.en: Understand the meaning, branches and importance of general knowledge.
description.rw: Sobanukirwa igisobanuro, amashami n'akamaro k'ubumenyi rusange.

definition.en: General knowledge is a broad understanding of information from different subjects, including science, history, geography, culture, society and technology.
definition.rw: Ubumenyi rusange ni ugusobanukirwa amakuru aturuka mu masomo atandukanye arimo siyansi, amateka, geografiya, umuco, sosiyete n'ikoranabuhanga.

body.en:
General knowledge helps people understand the world and make informed decisions. It includes knowledge about natural processes, communities, countries, historical events and technological developments.

Science explains natural phenomena through observation and evidence. Geography studies places, people and environments. History examines past events and their effects on societies. Technology explores tools and systems used to solve problems. Civics and culture help people understand responsibilities, shared values and social relationships.

Reliable learning requires more than memorising facts. Learners should compare information, ask questions, examine evidence and distinguish verified facts from opinions. Educational materials from recognised institutions are useful starting points.
body.rw:
Ubumenyi rusange bufasha abantu gusobanukirwa isi no gufata ibyemezo bishingiye ku makuru. Burimo ubumenyi ku mikorere ya kamere, imiryango, ibihugu, ibyabaye mu mateka n'iterambere ry'ikoranabuhanga.

Siyansi isobanura ibibera muri kamere ikoresheje kwitegereza n'ibimenyetso. Geografiya yiga ahantu, abantu n'ibidukikije. Amateka yiga ibyabaye kera n'ingaruka byagize ku miryango. Ikoranabuhanga ryiga ibikoresho na sisitemu bikoreshwa mu gukemura ibibazo. Ubumenyi ku miyoborere n'umuco bufasha gusobanukirwa inshingano, indangagaciro n'imibanire.

Kwiga mu buryo bwizewe ntibisaba gufata mu mutwe amakuru gusa. Umunyeshuri agomba kugereranya amakuru, kubaza ibibazo, gusuzuma ibimenyetso no gutandukanya ukuri kwagenzuwe n'ibitekerezo. Inyandiko z'uburezi zituruka mu bigo byemewe ni ahantu heza ho gutangirira.

en: General knowledge covers many subjects.
Reliable information should be checked.
Learning requires questions and evidence.
Facts and opinions are not the same.
Knowledge supports responsible decisions.
rw: Kwiga bisaba kubaza ibibazo no gusuzuma ibimenyetso.

conclusion.en: General knowledge develops understanding, critical thinking and the ability to make responsible decisions.
conclusion.rw: Ubumenyi rusange buteza imbere gusobanukirwa, gutekereza neza no gufata ibyemezo bishinzwe.

quiz_connection.en: Be able to explain the meaning of general knowledge and identify its main subject areas.
quiz_connection.rw: Ugomba gusobanura igisobanuro cy'ubumenyi rusange no kugaragaza amasomo y'ingenzi bukubiyemo.

content.en:
DEFINITION
General knowledge is an understanding of information from many different fields.

DETAILED LESSON
It includes science, geography, history, culture and technology. General knowledge helps people understand society and make informed decisions. Reliable learning involves checking sources, comparing evidence and distinguishing facts from opinions. It is useful to read educational materials from recognised institutions.

CONCLUSION
Continuous learning builds knowledge and improves critical thinking.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Ubumenyi rusange ni ugusobanukirwa amakuru aturuka mu nzego n'amasomo atandukanye.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Bukubiyemo siyansi, geografiya, amateka, umuco n'ikoranabuhanga. Bufasha abantu gusobanukirwa sosiyete no gufata ibyemezo bishingiye ku makuru. Kwiga mu buryo bwizewe bisaba kugenzura inkomoko y'amakuru, kugereranya ibimenyetso no gutandukanya ukuri n'ibitekerezo. Ni byiza gusoma inyandiko z'uburezi zituruka mu bigo byemewe.

UMWANZURO
Gukomeza kwiga byongera ubumenyi kandi bigateza imbere ubushobozi bwo gutekereza neza.

description.en: Explore the Earth's physical features, continents, oceans and human geography.
description.rw: Menya imiterere y'isi, imigabane, inyanja na geografiya y'abantu.

definition.en: Geography is the study of the Earth, its physical features, people, places, environments and the relationships between them.
definition.rw: Geografiya ni isomo ryiga isi, imiterere yayo, abantu, ahantu, ibidukikije n'isano biri hagati yabyo.

body.en:
Physical geography studies natural features such as mountains, rivers, lakes, plains, deserts and climate. Human geography studies population, settlements, languages, economic activities and transport.

Maps represent places and spatial relationships. A map may show political boundaries, roads, rivers, relief or population distribution. A globe represents the Earth in a three-dimensional form. Latitude and longitude help identify locations.

Africa is one of the world's continents, and Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa. Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda. Geography helps people understand the relationship between communities, resources, climate and development.
body.rw:
Geografiya y'imiterere karemano yiga ibintu nk'imisozi, imigezi, ibiyaga, ibibaya, ubutayu n'ikirere. Geografiya y'abantu yiga umubare w'abaturage, aho batuye, indimi, ibikorwa by'ubukungu n'ubwikorezi.

Ikarita igaragaza ahantu n'isano hagati y'ahantu hatandukanye. Ikarita ishobora kwerekana imbibi z'ibihugu, imihanda, imigezi, imiterere y'ubutaka cyangwa uko abaturage bakwirakwiye. Umubumbe w'isi werekana isi mu buryo bw'umuzenguruko. Imirongo y'uburinganire n'iy'uburebure ifasha kumenya aho ahantu haherereye.

Afurika ni umwe mu migabane y'isi, naho u Rwanda rukaba igihugu kitagira inkombe z'inyanja giherereye muri Afurika y'Iburasirazuba. Kigali ni umurwa mukuru w'u Rwanda. Geografiya ifasha gusobanukirwa isano iri hagati y'abaturage, umutungo kamere, ikirere n'iterambere.

en: Geography studies people, places and environments.
Physical geography studies natural features.
Human geography studies people and activities.
Maps and globes help identify locations.
Rwanda is in East Africa and Kigali is its capital.
rw: Geografiya y'abantu yiga abantu n'ibikorwa byabo.
u Rwanda ruri muri Afurika y'Iburasirazuba kandi Kigali ni umurwa mukuru.

conclusion.en: Geography helps explain how the Earth works and how people interact with their surroundings.
conclusion.rw: Geografiya ifasha gusobanukirwa imikorere y'isi n'uko abantu babana n'ibidukikije.

quiz_connection.en: Identify geography's main branches and explain the difference between physical and human geography.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya amashami ya geografiya kandi usobanure itandukaniro riri hagati ya geografiya karemano n'iy'abantu.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Geography studies the Earth, its people, places and environments.

DETAILED LESSON
Physical geography examines mountains, rivers, lakes and climate. Human geography examines population, settlements, transport and economic activities. Maps and globes help identify locations. Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa, and Kigali is its capital.

CONCLUSION
Geography improves our understanding of the relationship between people and their environment.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Geografiya yiga isi, abantu bayituyeho, ahantu n'ibidukikije.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Geografiya karemano yiga imisozi, imigezi, ibiyaga n'ikirere. Geografiya y'abantu yiga abaturage, aho batuye, ubwikorezi n'ibikorwa by'ubukungu. Amakarita n'imibumbe bifasha kumenya ahantu. u Rwanda ni igihugu kitagira inkombe z'inyanja giherereye muri Afurika y'Iburasirazuba, kandi Kigali ni umurwa mukuru warwo.

UMWANZURO
Geografiya ituma turushaho gusobanukirwa isano iri hagati y'abantu n'ibidukikije.

title.en: Introduction to Science and Scientific Thinking
title.rw: Intangiriro kuri siyansi no gutekereza gushingiye ku bumenyi

description.en: Learn what science is, how evidence is used and why scientific knowledge develops.
description.rw: Menya siyansi icyo ari cyo, uko ibimenyetso bikoreshwa n'impamvu ubumenyi bwa siyansi butera imbere.

definition.en: Science is a systematic process of studying the natural and physical world through observation, questions, investigation and evidence.
definition.rw: Siyansi ni uburyo buteguye bwo kwiga ibibera muri kamere no mu isi hakoreshejwe kwitegereza, kubaza ibibazo, gukora ubushakashatsi no gusuzuma ibimenyetso.

body.en:
Scientific investigation often begins with a question about something observed. A researcher identifies what is being studied, develops a possible explanation and gathers evidence. The evidence is then examined to determine whether it supports the explanation.

Biology studies living organisms. Chemistry studies substances and how they change. Physics examines matter, energy and forces. Earth science studies the planet and its natural systems. These fields contribute to medicine, agriculture, engineering and environmental protection.

Scientific conclusions should be based on evidence rather than personal belief alone. Scientific knowledge can be improved when new reliable evidence becomes available. Learners should distinguish scientific evidence from unsupported claims.
body.rw:
Ubushakashatsi bwa siyansi akenshi butangirana n'ikibazo kijyanye n'ikintu cyabonetse cyangwa cyitegerejwe. Umushakashatsi amenya icyo agiye kwiga, agatanga igisobanuro gishoboka hanyuma agakora ubushakashatsi kugira ngo abone ibimenyetso. Ibyo bimenyetso birasuzumwa kugira ngo hamenyekane niba bishyigikira igisobanuro yatangiye atanga.

Ibinyabuzima byiga ibinyabuzima biriho. Ubutabire bwiga ibintu n'uko bihinduka. Ubugenge bwiga ibintu, ingufu n'imbaraga. Ubumenyi bw'isi bwiga umubumbe w'isi n'imikorere ya kamere. Aya mashami afasha mu buvuzi, ubuhinzi, ubwubatsi n'ukurengera ibidukikije.

Imyanzuro ya siyansi igomba gushingira ku bimenyetso aho gushingira ku myemerere y'umuntu gusa. Ubumenyi bwa siyansi bushobora kunozwa iyo habonetse ibimenyetso bishya byizewe. Abanyeshuri bagomba gutandukanya ibimenyetso bya siyansi n'ibivugwa bidafite gihamya.

en: Science uses observation and evidence.
Biology studies living organisms.
Chemistry studies substances and changes.
Physics studies matter, energy and forces.
Scientific knowledge develops with reliable evidence.
rw: Ubumenyi bwa siyansi butera imbere hakurikijwe ibimenyetso byizewe.

conclusion.en: Science develops reliable explanations through investigation, observation and evidence.
conclusion.rw: Siyansi itanga ibisobanuro byizewe binyuze mu bushakashatsi, kwitegereza no gusuzuma ibimenyetso.

quiz_connection.en: Identify the main branches of science and explain why evidence is important in scientific investigations.
quiz_connection.rw: Menya amashami y'ingenzi ya siyansi kandi usobanure impamvu ibimenyetso ari ingenzi mu bushakashatsi.

content.en:
DEFINITION
Science is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and evidence.

DETAILED LESSON
Science includes biology, chemistry, physics and earth science. Scientific investigation involves asking questions, observing, gathering information and examining evidence. Scientific explanations can improve when reliable new evidence becomes available.

CONCLUSION
Scientific thinking helps people understand the world and make decisions based on evidence.
content.rw:
IGISOBANURO
Siyansi ni uburyo buteguye bwo kwiga ibibera muri kamere hakoreshejwe kwitegereza n'ibimenyetso.

ISOMO RIRAMBUYE
Siyansi ikubiyemo ibinyabuzima, ubutabire, ubugenge n'ubumenyi bw'isi. Ubushakashatsi bwa siyansi burimo kubaza ibibazo, kwitegereza, gukusanya amakuru no gusuzuma ibimenyetso. Ibisobanuro bya siyansi bishobora kunozwa iyo habonetse ibimenyetso bishya byizewe.

UMWANZURO
Gutekereza gushingiye kuri siyansi bifasha gusobanukirwa isi no gufata ibyemezo bishingiye ku bimenyetso.
